verdicts.decisive_quote: The most recent reported quarter (Q1 2025) showed strong revenue growth and earnings beat, but guidance missed expectations. The exact year-over-year revenue growth percentage for Q1 2025 is not available.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: The only trace that refuses to invent the missing Q1 figure: every claim it makes (guidance miss, the 6% global ad-forecast cut, WhatsApp ads launch) maps to an E1 headline, the mass is held at a moderate 0.70 against a declared magnitude gap, but it silently rewrites the target as a 16.07 percentage-point acceleration and that reframing does much of the work behind 'no'.

verdicts.decisive_quote: Meta Platforms Inc. reported strong revenue growth in Q1 2025, with year-over-year growth at 27%, indicating a robust underlying business performance and exceeding the target threshold.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Best mechanism inventory of the seven (WhatsApp ads, AI capex payoff, WPP's 6% cut, the guidance miss, all real E1 headlines) but the 27% Q1 anchor appears nowhere in E1 or its retrieved factors, and the trip from that anchor down to a 15.0% central estimate — below the boundary — is asserted, with a global ad-market rate used as if it bounded Meta's own.

verdicts.decisive_quote: The forecast is 'no' because while growth is indicated as strong, there is insufficient specific evidence to confirm it will reach or surpass the 16.07 threshold.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Invents nothing and matches near-uniform mass (0.51/0.49) to a genuinely undecidable read of headline-only evidence, but the reasoning block states 'no' while the forecast emits 'yes' via a boundary-centered abstention — the label is the opposite of what the trace argued.

verdicts.decisive_quote: The evidence directly supports Meta's revenue growth metric and provides recent performance data (Q1 2025) and forward-looking projections that indicate strong growth, supporting the magnitude of the estimate.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Cleanly maps its reasoning onto 'yes' and says why 'no' is excluded, but calls its magnitude support 'direct' when every cited E0 item is a bare headline with no figure, then builds a 17/22/28 percent band on 'analyst projections' that do not exist in the bank and puts 0.9 behind it.

verdicts.decisive_quote: Given the consistently positive indicators and strong Q1 performance, it is highly probable that Meta will achieve this threshold in Q2 2025.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: The only trace to state the full resolution rule (level at least 16.07 percent AND at least the prior quarter's growth), yet it assigns 0.9 to clearing that boundary from headlines containing no revenue figure at all, attributes Reels monetization and AI ad targeting to a Business Insider headline that says neither, and admits no gap anywhere.

verdicts.decisive_quote: Meta Platforms, Inc. reported strong year-over-year revenue growth of approximately 27% in the first quarter of 2025.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: The entire conclusion rests on a fabricated 27% Q1 2025 figure cited to three E0 snippets that carry no numbers (its retrieved memory offers only 23% for Q3 2023 and 25% for Q4 2023), and that invented anchor is what makes 'no' look 'highly improbable' at 0.85.

verdicts.decisive_quote: "low": 0.0, "central": 8.0, "high": 15.0, "unit": "percent", "basis": "Derived from general positive trends and Q1 2025 performance, with uncertainty due to lack of specific Q2 2025 YoY growth data."
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Declares its directional signal 'up' and every reasoning step positive, then produces a band whose upper bound lands one point under the boundary from a basis of 'general positive trends' — the interval, not the argument, delivers 'no', and confidence is raised from 0.55 to 0.75 between stages with no added support.

ranking_rationale: Neither bank contains a single revenue figure, so the separator was whether a trace admitted that and priced it, or filled the hole with a number: hgf states outright that the Q1 growth rate is unavailable and keeps mass moderate, while structure_memory and factor_memory manufacture a 27% Q1 anchor and case_memory relabels headline-only evidence as 'direct' magnitude support. Below the top, traces are split between those whose stated reasoning at least uniquely picks their option (case_memory, structure_memory) and those where the option is delivered by an unargued latent interval or contradicts the trace's own text (direct_forecast, principle_memory).
shared_evidence_note: Bank content mattered at the margin — only E1 carried the WPP 6% ad-forecast cut and the 'Guidance Misses Expectations' headline that pushed both E1 methods toward 'no' — but it does not explain the disagreement, since the five E0 methods split three ways (yes, no, and a boundary abstention) from an identical set of ten numberless headlines.
